lines.t: At three in the morning, a woman walked through London... shooting dried peas at people's windows.
And they paid her for it. Sixpence a week.
Back then, a good alarm clock cost too much. And if you were late to the factory, you could lose your job.
So she WAS the alarm clock. Her job title? Knocker-up.
Her tool: a long tube, and a pocket full of dried peas. Tak. Tak. Tak.
And she didn't leave until you came to the window.
Grumpy customers growled and banged things around. Happy ones tapped back, like a little song.
She even had a rival, three miles away. He used a fishing rod.
Others used long bamboo poles... or just whistled.
You see, a pea is the perfect alarm. Loud enough to wake you up. Too tiny to break the glass. And aimed at one window only.
Her daughter took over the job. And she kept shooting peas, even through the air raids of the war.
Then cheap alarm clocks showed up, and the job slowly disappeared.
But knocker-ups were the only people awake while the whole street slept.
So one night, when one of them spotted a house on fire...
they did the one thing they were paid to do. They woke everybody up.
Sixpence a week for a pea at your window. A, deal. Or B, I'll take my chances.
